events.summary: An independent opus-driven approval review of this branch (relayed by the coordinator, not self-run) returned REQUEST_CHANGES with 8 findings: 2 HIGH (D40/doc comment falsely claimed check_spawn_admission is wired into a spawn path; check_spawn_admission silently admitted on memory-probe failure instead of failing closed), 4 MEDIUM (GC guard read poisoned locks as "not protected"; GC guard missed non-canonical path aliases and in-progress training output dirs; mlx.rs duplicated access.rs's serving healthcheck; the original trace overclaimed live verification), 2 LOW (error text said "4bit" for any quantization width; mlx.rs's line count and mixed pure/glue logic). Each finding was checked against the actual code before fixing, none were disputed.
events.provenance: independent Claude Opus 5.5 approval-lane review, findings delivered verbatim by the coordinator in-session

events.summary: Fixed all 8 review findings across 5 new commits, staying inside the original re-land's boundary: #32/53464bb (wiring check_spawn_admission into a real spawn path) remains explicitly out of scope and was not added. Touched only guardrails.rs, mlx.rs, access.rs (one function made pub(crate), no behavior change), two new services/ files, and src/types/ipc.ts (one additive field, not high-risk per risk-policy.json). docs/03-mvp-design.md D40 row corrected for truthfulness only.

Findings 1+2 (HIGH): rewrote the D40 doc row and check_spawn_admission's doc comment to state plainly that the gate is unwired dead code, not enforced; made check_spawn_admission fail closed on memory_pressure_level == "unknown" (probe failure) while leaving thermal_state: None pass-through unchanged. Finding 5 (MEDIUM): made access.rs::check_serving_health pub(crate) and had mlx.rs::is_serving_healthy delegate to it instead of duplicating the curl call. Findings 3+4 (MEDIUM): is_adapter_safe_to_delete now returns false (not "safe") on any poisoned MlxState lock instead of treating lock failure as "not protected"; path comparisons now go through canonicalize (falls back to the raw path when canonicalize fails, e.g. path doesn't exist) so a non-canonical alias of the serving/last-known-good adapter is still caught; added TrainingStatus.adapter_name (known from spawn, unlike adapter_path which is only set at "done") so an in-progress training run's output directory is protected too. Finding 8 (LOW): generalized the rejection error text beyond "4bit" and added detection of a quantization_config key (top-level or under text_config) alongside the existing quantization key; checked real config.json files under ~/.cache/huggingface on this machine (mlx-community/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct-4bit uses only top-level quantization; no quantization_config example was found locally, so that branch is defensive per the review, not observed).

Finding 7 (LOW): extracted the pure decision logic behind #12 (last-known-good) and #33 (checkpoint status / GC guard) into two new files, services/mlx_artifacts.rs and services/mlx_serving_recovery.rs, neither depending on MlxState or tauri. mlx.rs keeps thin call sites that lock MlxState's Mutexes, extract plain values, and delegate to the pure functions; the poisoned-lock fail-closed behavior stays in mlx.rs since only it holds the Mutex. No behavior change — every pre-existing test still passes against the refactored wrappers, plus 8 new pure-logic tests were added directly in the two service modules.

cargo test --lib after all 5 review-round commits: 164 passed, 0 failed (up from 144 at the initial re-land: +2 guardrails unknown-memory tests, +3 GC-guard alias/in-progress/poisoned-lock tests, +2 quantization_config fixture tests, +8 new pure-logic tests split across services::mlx_artifacts and services::mlx_serving_recovery, plus the pre-existing tests carried through the refactor unmodified)

events.summary: Done means: the re-land plus all 8 review findings compile, pass the full unit test suite (164/164), and pass every lint/build/license gate. This is explicitly NOT a claim that check_spawn_admission, the last-known-good health-poll loop (record_last_known_good_after_healthcheck), is_adapter_safe_to_delete/manifest_verification_status, or reject_incompatible_runtime_combo have been exercised against a live colima cluster, a running mlx-lm/mlx-vlm server, or a real fine-tuning process — none of them are: check_spawn_admission has no caller anywhere (wiring is #32, still out of scope); the health-poll loop requires a live serving process and an AppHandle and was only reasoned about, never run; the GC guard and manifest status functions have no IPC registration and were only exercised through unit fixtures (temp directories, synthetic config.json files); reject_incompatible_runtime_combo was only exercised against fixture config.json files, not a real spawn attempt. This mirrors the original re-land's scope — this review round did not add any new runtime exercise, only unit-level correctness fixes and tests.

Complete and verified for the re-land + review-fix scope: backend logic compiles, all 164 unit tests pass, and every lint/license/build gate passes. Runtime verification of the admission gate, health-poll loop, and GC guard against a live process remains unexercised by design, since none of them are wired into a live spawn/serving path in this scope (wiring stays #32/53464bb, explicitly out of scope in both the original instructions and this review round).
